_metadata.description: Restructured questionnaire based on workshop feedback suggestions

info.title: InsectAI hardware database
info.description:
A questionnaire to collect information about automated insect monitoring hardware devices for the InsectAI COST Action hardware database. 
 At the moment, only optical systems (i.e that use cameras) are supported. 

 Only the basic details about an entry are mandatory, (i.e. new/update submission, contact name, email, device name and description). Following the basic info, there are several technical questions intended to guide you in reporting important information about the hardware, but they are all skippable, and not everything will be relevant for all devices. 
  Filling in the questionnaire should not take longer than a half hour.  

 For more details see: https://github.com/InsectAI-COST-Action/hardware-db

questions.title: Do you want to submit a new device, or update an existing entry?
questions.description:
Unsure if you have already submitted? 

 Important: this name will be used as a basis to create a unique deviceID in the database; if a record for a deviceID already exists, it will be overwritten (this can be reversed by database maintainers). 

 You can check what has already been submitted to the database here: https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

sections.title: Basic information
sections.description:
Core details about the device and its contact person. 

 Important: all this information will be publicly accessible!

questions.title: Contact person name
questions.description: The person who should be contacted about this database entry. This does not have to be the device designer: it can be a user, project manager, lab lead, or maintainer.

questions.title: Contact email
questions.description:
A valid email address (e.g. name@institution.org) for the contact person above. 

 Please note this email address will be publicly visible!

questions.title: Institutional affiliation(s) of the contact person
questions.description:
The institution name(s) that the contact person is affiliated with, no address needed. 

 Please separate multiple affiliations with ';'.

questions.title: Device name
questions.description:
The common or published name of the device (e.g. 'AMI-trap', 'InsectDetect', 'PitfallCam'). If the device has no established name, use a short descriptive label. 

 Important: this name will be used as a basis to create a unique deviceID in the database; if a record for a deviceID already exists, it will be overwritten (this can be reversed by database maintainers). 

 You can check for existing deviceID using ths page: https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

questions.title: Device description
questions.description: A short abstract (max 300 characters) explaining what the device is and does, for a non-specialist audience. Focus on purpose and key features rather than technical specifications here.

sections.title: Technical questions
sections.description:
In the following sections there are several technical questions. 
 They are all skippable, and we DO NOT expect that you will be able to fill in every single one! 
 They are intended as a guide to help you report important information about your hardware. 

 When you are ready to submit, navigate to the end of the questionnaire and click 'Submit'.

sections.title: People and project details
sections.description: Information about the people involved in using, designing, building, and/or maintaining the device.

questions.title: Team size
questions.description: How many people are part of the team responsible for the device?

questions.title: Person hours
questions.description: Approximately, how many Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs) were committed to working with or on the device? Select the appropriate range (e.g. 1 person full-time, 1 person 60% = 1.6 FTE, select '1-2 FTEs')

questions.title: Project duration
questions.description: What is / was the overall duration of the project that this device was developed or used in?

questions.title: Contributor name
questions.description: May differ from the contact person or device creator if someone else is submitting on their behalf.

questions.title: Contributor email
questions.description:
Email of the person filling in this form. 
 If it would be the same as the contact person's, simply leave blank.

questions.title: Contributor role
questions.description:
Role of the person submitting this form 

 Select between: 
Project lead: directs the project (e.g. PI, lab lead)
Hardware developer: designed or built the device hardware
Software developer: wrote device firmware or software
Field researcher or practitioner: deploys or operates the device in the field
Technician: handles assembly, maintenance, or repair
Data manager: processes or curates data from the device

questions.title: Team member 1 - Name
questions.description: Full name of a person involved in the project.

questions.title: Team member 1 - Affiliation(s)
questions.description: Institution(s) this person is affiliated with. Separate multiple with ';'.

questions.title: Team member 1 - Role
questions.description: Select the role that best describes this person's involvement with the device.

questions.title: Team member 2 - Affiliation(s)
questions.description: Separate multiple with ';'.

questions.title: Team member 3 - Affiliation(s)
questions.description: Separate multiple with ';'.

questions.title: Team member 4 - Affiliation(s)
questions.description: Separate multiple with ';'.

questions.title: Team member 5 - Affiliation(s)
questions.description: Separate multiple with ';'.

questions.title: Additional team members
questions.description:
Here you can list any additional team members, their affiliation and their role. 
 Please separate name, affiliation and role using ';', and separate team member entries with '|'. 
 For example: 'Name Surname; Affiliation 1, Affiliation 2; Role | Name Surname; Affiliation 1; Role' and so on

sections.title: Device links and documentation
sections.description: Links to external documentation, publications, and resources. We cannot host files directly — please provide URLs to externally hosted content (e.g. GitHub, Zenodo, institutional repositories).

questions.title: Documentation URL
questions.description: Link to the main documentation or repository for this device (e.g. GitHub repo, wiki, or project page).

questions.title: Documentation language
questions.description: Primary language(s) of the documentation; if multilingual please separate wih ';' (e.g. 'English'; 'French'; 'Spanish')

questions.title: DOI(s)
questions.description: Digital Object Identifier(s) for publications related to this device. Separate multiple DOIs with ';' (e.g. '10.1234/example1; 10.5678/example2').

questions.title: Additional resources
questions.description: Links to other relevant resources such as video tutorials, YouTube channels, blog posts, or community forums. Separate multiple URLs with ';'.

sections.title: Device details
sections.description: Physical characteristics, construction, and cost information for the device.

questions.title: Device construction
questions.description: Select all that apply.
options: Modified off-the-shelf: Pre-built device with user-made adjustments
Partly custom: Assembled from off-the-shelf/open-source components with some user design (e.g. 3D-printed parts)
Fully custom: Designed and fabricated entirely by the user (e.g custom PCB)

questions.title: Unit build cost (€) — hardware only
questions.description: Approximate cost of components, electronics, enclosure, etc. for one unit.

questions.title: Deployment/seasonal costs (€/season)
questions.description: Consumables per deployment or season (batteries, lures, SIM data, etc.).

questions.title: Ongoing software/compute costs (€/year)
questions.description: Cloud services, subscriptions, or compute costs per year (if applicable).

questions.title: Assembly time/cost
questions.description: Estimated human-hours to assemble one unit (e.g. '4 hours', '2 days').

questions.title: Packaged dimensions for transport (L × W × H)
questions.description: Approximate dimensions in mm when the device is packed for transport (e.g. '300 × 200 × 150').

questions.title: Deployed dimensions (L × W × H)
questions.description: Approximate dimensions in mm when the device is set up and operational (e.g. '500 × 400 × 800').

questions.title: Weight (kg)
questions.description: Approximate weight of one complete unit, including batteries, supports, fasteners, solar panel, etc.

questions.title: Skills and tools required for construction
questions.description: Select all skills/tools needed to build or assemble the device.

questions.title: Device version name
questions.description: A label for this specific version of the device (e.g. 'v2.1', '2024-field-edition'). Useful when multiple versions exist.

questions.title: Device licence (e.g. CC-BY-4.0)
questions.description: The licence under which the device design is released. Use a standard SPDX identifier where possible (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0', 'CERN-OHL-S-2.0'). Leave blank if unknown.

sections.title: Component details
sections.description: Technical specifications of the device's sensors, power system, processing, and connectivity.

questions.title: Power source(s)
questions.description: Select all power sources that can be used to operate the device.

questions.title: Power autonomy under continuous use
questions.description:
How long the device can run on a single charge/battery set during continuous operation (e.g. '8 hours', '3 days'). 
 If fully autonomous (e.g. solar panels), report the longest period a unit has been left unattended and was functioning. Leave blank if grid-powered only.

questions.title: Processing unit
questions.description: The main compute component (e.g. 'Raspberry Pi 4', 'NVIDIA Jetson Nano', 'Arduino Uno', 'ESP32'). Include model and version where known.

questions.title: AI model processing
questions.description: Where detection or classification AI models are run. Select all that apply.
options: Offboard processing (data transfer to separate computer)

questions.title: Available image capture modes
questions.description: Select all image/video capture modes supported by the device.

questions.title: Main optical sensor model name, if known
Main sensor resolution.
questions.description: If multiple resolutions are supported, please choose the closest typical output resolution.

questions.title: Main sensor frame-rate (frames per second, fps)
questions.description: If multiple frame-rates are supported, choose the most commonly used during deployment.

questions.title: Minimum focal distance (closest focus distance)
questions.description: Closest distance at which the camera can focus sharply on the target.

questions.title: Sensor/lens field of view (FoV)
questions.description: The angular field of view of the main imaging sensor, if known (e.g. '120°', '62° horizontal').

questions.title: Connectivity options
questions.description: Select all connectivity options available on the device.

questions.title: Supported file types
questions.description: Select all data file types produced by the device.

sections.title: Maintenance and repairs
sections.description: Information about device upkeep, repairability, and firmware updates.

questions.title: Maintenance interval
questions.description: How often routine maintenance is needed (e.g. 'Clean lens every 2 weeks', 'Replace desiccant monthly', 'Battery swap every 3 days').

questions.title: Repairability score (1 = very difficult, 5 = very easy)
questions.description: 1 = requires soldering or specialist tools; 2 = requires tools but no specialist skills; 3 = screwdriver assembly, standard parts; 4 = snap-fit or modular replacement; 5 = fully tool-free, hot-swap components.

questions.title: Date of last firmware/software update
questions.description: Approximate date of the most recent firmware or software update (e.g. 'January 2026').

questions.title: Firmware update method
questions.description: Select all methods by which firmware can be updated on this device.

questions.title: On-device software or firmware version and repository link
questions.description: Version of the software or firmware running on the device and a link to its source repository, if available, use '|' as separator (e.g. 'v1.3.2 | https://github.com/org/repo').

sections.title: Intended usage scope and operational constraints
sections.description: Information about where, how, and for what organisms the device is designed to be used.

questions.title: Does this device target organisms primarily by taxonomic identity or functional group?
questions.description:
Taxonomic: the device is designed to detect and/or classify organisms by species or higher taxonomic rank (e.g. genus, family, order). 
Functional: the device is designed to detect or classify organisms by ecological role or trait (e.g. pollinators, nocturnal insects). 
Both: the device supports or has been used for both approaches.
options: Taxonomic groups (species, genus, family, order, etc.)

questions.title: Target taxonomic group(s)
questions.description: Select all taxonomic groups this device is designed or validated for.

questions.title: Target functional group(s)
questions.description: Select all functional groups that device is designed or has been used to record.
options: Decomposers / detritivores (e.g. dung beetles, carrion feeders)

questions.title: Habitat type(s)
questions.description: Select all habitat types where this device is designed to operate.

questions.title: Operational environment
questions.description: The broad environment category for device deployment.

questions.title: Attractants used
questions.description: Select all attractants employed by the device. Attractants are used to draw insects toward the sensor.

questions.title: Minimum operational temperature (°C)
questions.description: The lowest ambient temperature at which the device functions reliably.

questions.title: Maximum operational temperature (°C)
questions.description: The highest ambient temperature at which the device functions reliably.

questions.title: IP rating (weatherproofing)
questions.description: The Ingress Protection rating, if known (e.g. 'IP65', 'IP67'); see here for more details: https://www.iec.ch/ip-ratings. If no formal rating, describe the protection and estimate the closest IP rating (e.g. 'splash-proof enclosure, IP64', 'fully sealed, IP68').

questions.title: Minimum detectable subject size (mm)
questions.description: The smallest organism or object size the device can reliably detect or image (in mm).

questions.title: Maximum detectable subject size (mm)
questions.description: The largest organism or object size the device is designed to capture (in mm). Leave blank if not applicable.
